conclusions: The insider-sponsorship statement is the strongest verified personally inconvenient fact.
The litigation is the strongest severe allegation but remains unproven and plaintiff-controlled.
The most defensible criticism is operational and managerial rather than criminal corruption.
Do not label Leatherman corrupt on the current record.
counterarguments: Strong sponsorship can reflect merit rather than favoritism.
Cyber takedowns are designed to impose costs and gather intelligence, not necessarily achieve permanent elimination in one action.
Salt Typhoon responsibility was distributed across agencies, telecom carriers and technology vendors.
findings: A former FBI Cyber Division selecting official publicly said he double promoted Leatherman over candidates with more tenure and predicted his eventual rise to assistant director.
A pending federal lawsuit names Leatherman and alleges surveillance, harassment, evidence misconduct and abuse of authority; no merits finding substantiating the allegations was identified.
LockBit restored public infrastructure within five days of Operation Cronos, limiting any permanent-takedown narrative even though the operation later damaged LockBit's trust and activity.
BreachForums repeatedly reappeared after FBI-led seizures, illustrating the displacement limits of the disruption strategy Leatherman publicly champions.

Salt Typhoon operated for years and compromised telecom and lawful-intercept information, creating leadership-accountability exposure in Leatherman's mission portfolio without establishing personal causation.
No verified bribery, illicit payment, campaign-finance link, adjudicated corruption finding or direct personal WEF role was identified.
limitations: Full PACER docket and sealed investigative records were unavailable.
No non-public personnel, disciplinary or financial disclosure records were reviewed.
Absence of a finding is not proof that no undisclosed matter exists.
